article_title: The effectiveness of problem-based learning in pediatric medical education in China: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
citation: Ma Yimei MM, Lu Xiaoxi MD, Hayashi Shogo. (2019). The effectiveness of problem-based learning in pediatric medical education in China: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000014052
title: Meta-analysis corpus of 12 RCTs comparing PBL and LBL in Chinese pediatric medical education
description: A corpus of 12 randomized controlled trials including 1003 medical students, comparing PBL with LBL in pediatric medical education in China. The search covered Chinese databases (CNKI, WanFang, China Science Periodical Database, Chinese BioMedical Literature Database) and English databases (PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central), "from inception up to June 2018". Courses included pediatric teaching, pediatric nervous system diseases, and pediatric clinical practice; sample sizes ranged from 20 to 68.
requirements: Studies compared PBL teaching in the experimental group with LBL teaching in the control group in pediatric medical education in China
Outcome measures were theoretical knowledge scores, skill scores, or case analysis scores
constraints: Only Chinese medical students were included, so the authors state the results "may have limited geographical generalization"
No subgroup analysis by course type was performed because of incomplete data
examples: 317 potentially relevant studies were identified; 305 were excluded at screening, leaving 12 RCTs published between 2007 and 2017
key_sources: Ma Yimei MM, Lu Xiaoxi MD, Hayashi Shogo. (2019). The effectiveness of problem-based learning in pediatric medical education in China: A meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000014052

article_title: The reliability of answers from four different AI chatbots on periodontology theoretical exam questions: an evaluation in dental education.
citation: Koyuncuoglu Cenker Zeki, Selcuker Ahmet Hamdi, Ozyilmaz Erdem. (2025). The reliability of answers from four different AI chatbots on periodontology theoretical exam questions: an evaluation in dental education. BMC Oral Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12903-025-07387-z
title: 125-question periodontology exam question set from Istanbul Aydin University (2018–2023)
description: A set of 125 closed-ended questions retrieved from the official archives of the Department of Periodontology, Faculty of Dentistry, Istanbul Aydin University, originally included in exams given to 3rd, 4th, and 5th-year students between 2018 and 2023. The article reports "92 of the questions are true/false, 8 are fill-in-the-blank, 22 are multiple-choice, and 3 are calculation questions"; 25 repeated questions were removed. Answers were scored on a binary 1–0 scale against faculty-validated official answer keys.
requirements: Closed-ended format with clearly defined correct answers for objective evaluation
constraints: Questions are archived at the department and not publicly accessible; may be provided upon formal request
The study did not evaluate references used by the chatbots or closeness of incorrect answers
examples: Example items include a true/false question on the junctional epithelium, a fill-in-the-blank suture-thickness question, and a multiple-choice question on dentoalveolar fiber groups of the periodontal ligament
key_sources: Koyuncuoglu Cenker Zeki, Selcuker Ahmet Hamdi, Ozyilmaz Erdem. (2025). The reliability of answers from four different AI chatbots on periodontology theoretical exam questions: an evaluation in dental education. BMC Oral Health. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12903-025-07387-z

article_title: Evaluation of a 12-hole clock model for improving bronchoscopic skills in simulated normal and difficult airways among anesthesia residents: A randomized controlled study.
citation: Zhou Z, Zhang K, Zhao X, Hu Y, He Y, Wan L, Yao W. (2024). Evaluation of a 12-hole clock model for improving bronchoscopic skills in simulated normal and difficult airways among anesthesia residents: A randomized controlled study. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000038510
title: 12-hole clock model: a nonanatomical task trainer for fiberoptic bronchoscope manipulation
description: A patented (ZL201921518855.8), low-cost physical trainer with two layers: after passing the first-layer hole, the bronchoscope reaches a second layer where "12 holes are arranged in a circle, as in a standard 12-hour clock." Trainees steer the FOB tip to target holes in sequence (1st to 12th), linking manipulation to the familiar clock concept; the transparent exterior lets trainees observe FOB movement from outside. A two-ended assembly enables simultaneous use by two trainees in head-to-head competition.
requirements: Requires a flexible fibreoptic bronchoscope and trainees without prior bronchoscopic manipulation experience for novice training use
constraints: It is a nonanatomical task trainer focused on manipulation, separated from learning anatomy
The study's training course did not involve placement of a tracheal tube under FOB guidance
target_learners: anesthesia residents in their 1st or 2nd year of training without bronchoscopic intubation experience
target_learning_goals: fiberoptic bronchoscope manipulation and direction/angle control
preparation for bronchoscopic intubation in difficult airways
examples: In the trial, intervention participants manipulated the FOB sequentially from the 1st to 12th hole for 60 minutes with real-time guidance from two experienced anesthesiologists
key_sources: Zhou Z, Zhang K, Zhao X, Hu Y, He Y, Wan L, Yao W. (2024). Evaluation of a 12-hole clock model for improving bronchoscopic skills in simulated normal and difficult airways among anesthesia residents: A randomized controlled study. Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000038510
